sources.entry: WYGIWYH - Simple and powerful finance tracker. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: WYGIWYH is a self-hostable, opinionated personal finance tracker built around a no-budget "use what you earn this month" philosophy, with multi-currency support and a dollar-cost averaging tracker.
summary.what_it_does: It records income and expenses as transactions across multiple accounts (banks, wallets, investments) and supports multiple currencies, including user-defined custom currencies for crypto or rewards points. Custom rules can automatically adjust transactions, for example to handle credit card billing cycles. A built-in DCA tracker follows recurring investments such as crypto and stocks. It exposes an API for automations, with user-bound API tokens created via a management command, and can use OpenID Connect (OIDC) login through django-allauth. The README also describes an OAuth authorization server setup for remote MCP servers. It is deployed with Docker Compose and requires a PostgreSQL database; configuration is done through environment variables.
use_cases: track personal income and expenses in one place
manage multiple currencies in a finance tracker
track crypto or stock dollar-cost averaging
self-host a personal finance web app
automate transaction imports via API or n8n
log in to a finance app with OIDC single sign-on
how_to_run: Create docker-compose.yml from the project's example and fill in a .env file with your configuration
Create the first admin: docker compose exec -it web python manage.py createsuperuser
For local runs, remove URL, set HTTPS_ENABLED=false, and keep the default DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS
Unraid users can install the app from the Unraid Store instead (requires their own PostgreSQL 15+)
notable: Opinionated 'no-budget' philosophy: savings are tracked but not spent in later months, rather than enforcing budgets
Built-in dollar-cost averaging (DCA) tracker for recurring investments
User-defined custom currencies for crypto, reward points, or other models
Custom transaction rules for quirks like credit card billing cycles
Optional soft delete of transactions to help avoid duplicates during imports
caveats: The author states they are not an accountant, so some terms and calculations may be wrong
Not a budgeting or double-entry accounting application
Most calculations run at request time, which can slow pages as data grows (author reports around 500ms per page with 3000+ transactions)
The public demo wipes data every 24 hours or less and disables API, rules, automatic exchange rates, and import/export
